chunks: Ibn Abi Tayy al-Halabi said in the History of the Imamiyya:

(He is a sheikh from among the sheikhs of the Sufis, the tongue of the Imamiyya, the chief of kalam, fiqh, and dialectics. He used to debate the adherents of every creed while holding great standing in the Buyid state. He was generous in charitable donations, great in humility, abundant in salat and sawm, and excellent in dress.)

key_terms.الْجَدَلِ: Dialectics — the art of formal argumentation and disputation with theological opponents
key_terms.الْجَلَالَةِ: Grandeur/majesty — his lofty social and political standing in the Buyid court
key_terms.الْخُشُوعِ: Humility/reverence (khushu') — deep inward submissiveness before God
key_terms.لِسَانُ: Tongue — honorific title meaning 'spokesperson' or 'foremost voice' of the community

ai.seo_question: What does Ibn Abi Tayy al-Halabi say about the leading Shia scholar praised in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: Cited from Ibn Abi Tayy al-Halabi's History of the Imamiyya, this passage offers a panegyric portrait of a leading Shia scholar — praised for intellectual supremacy in kalam, fiqh, and dialectical disputation, as well as for personal piety. The scholar's distinguished standing within the Buyid state, broadly sympathetic to Shia Islam, underscores his socio-political prominence alongside his religious authority.
